feedback: The candidate faithfully encodes the five-milestone chain of the task (key B -> door B -> key A -> door A -> ball) as u0->u1->u2->u3->u4->u5, in the exact artifact format with a nonempty FINAL_STATES header (u5), which is declared in STATES and is accepting (reached precisely on target_ball_picked_up, the final-step milestone). Every state has a per-state else self-loop, so irrelevant or persistently true propositions (e.g., has_prerequisite_key lingering in u1, target_door_open persisting in u4, prerequisite_door_open persisting in u2/u3) are absorbed without spurious transitions or duplicate rewards. Regression handling is explicit exactly where the task requires it: (u1, required_key_lost) and (u3, required_key_lost) self-loops with -0.1 cover losing the currently gating key before its door opens, while re-pickups after a loss fall to else with no reward, preventing double reward farming. Determinism and completeness were verified against the environment constraints: required_key_lost requires empty hands and a currently closed door, so it cannot co-occur with the door_open pickup transitions (opening door A in u3 requires carrying key A) nor with the pickup transitions (which require carrying an object); the mutual-exclusion constraints (never two keys or key+ball held) keep all explicit labels within a state mutually exclusive. Reachability of u5 holds from every state even under setbacks (doors are never relocked, dropped keys can be re-picked), and the absorbing u5 with else is correct though the episode terminates at ball pickup. Rewards are dense across milestones (0.1 per milestone, 1.0 terminal), bounded, with only self-harming penalty accumulation possible (drop/re-pick cycles net negative), so reward safety holds. Minor note, not a defect: no penalty for required_key_lost in u2/u4 (dropping a key whose door is already opened, possibly re-shut); these are covered by else self-loops and are consistent with milestone semantics since the lost key no longer gates an unopened door.
